## Page 9

Business Group Performance
•Revenue spread across business groups  → Less reliance on 
revenue from its original core brands
•Lifestyle:  mainly Pandora (drastic decrease in the number of new 
products per collection released in Q1 2025, while Q2+Q3  internal 
operation adjustments led to better respond to customer needs ); 
Cath Kidston slightly lower sales despite closing 5 branches
•Fashion:  Strong sales growth (Marimekko plus new GANNI, United 
Arrows and MM6) ; Loss from sales of new store in Singapore not as 
planned in early stage (better development from Q2 2025 onward)
•Beauty & Wellness:  Sales growth from overseas; domestic drop 
from transfer of Online Cross -Border to China in Q1 2025 & 
significant drop in the number of tourists; Q3 2025 highest quarterly 
sales for China 
•F&B:  Sales growth from adding the 2nd branch of Bread Street 
Kitchen & Bar  at ICON Siam at the end of Q4 2024; Additional 
corporate/event/package sales and closing of lifestyle cafes on plan 
to reduce loss

•HARNN will be a major contributor in all countries.
•Target share of overseas revenue contribution is 15% and 25% in 2025 and 2026, respectively.

Selling Expense Q3 & 9M 2025
•Selling Expense & ratio to sales in Q3 2025 increased YoY mainly from
•More accumulated branches from expansion locally & abroad (rent, people, commission, fee & depreciation)

number of branches compared by quarter. This reflects the Group's ongoing efforts to control 
expenses.

## Page 14

General & Administrative Expense Q3 & 9M 2025
•G&A Expense in Q3 2025 included:
•Increased number of employees accumulated from year 2024 at head -office to support 
organization growth 
•Additional employee and office space overseas 
•Write -off of assets of Marimekko Kafé valued 2.2 million Baht
•9M 2025 G&A Expense increased YoY mainly from more accumulated employees locally and 
abroad, while r atio to Sales decreased YoY reflecting expense control in line with the business
Note: Q3 2024 included Unrealized Loss on Exchange Rate of 10.8 million Baht. Excluding this record Q3 2024  G&A expenses would be 65.4 million Baht and or 
15.9% to Sales. This year the Company has good control of expenses at similar level to last year even with more accumulated e mployees and offices.

## Page 15

Net Profit Q3 & 9M 2025
•Net Profit (Company) in Q3 2025 13.3 MB
•Overseas revenue growth YoY; but necessary to have selling and administrative expenses in each country that are balanced with  income
•Slight growth for Domestic revenue YoY → helped support the losses in the early stages of overseas operations
•Net Profit (Company) in 9M 2025 lower vs last year:
•Overseas revenues increased, selling and marketing expenses increased at a higher rate than sales growth in the short term.
•Unavoidable to take time to start a new business abroad
•However, losses of the Japanese business were clearly reduced significantly YoY.
•Contraction of domestic sales (aging society, a slowing economy, and politics that are not conducive to long -term economic growt h)
•Administrative expenses increased to support future growth of the business locally and internationally.
•The Group intends to build a larger business base to support future growth of the new business locally and internationally in  the long term.

## Page 20

Outlook 2025
•Long -term objective is to establish a solid and sustainable revenue base with consistent growth.
•Continue to prioritize brand development investments both domestically and internationally
•Expanding and strengthening our workforce to support increasingly diversified operations in the years ahead
•Reduce loss from overseas; further refine overseas management structure and operation
•Closure of underperforming branches as planned
•Key Digital Transformation initiatives — including the Line CRM with Rewards Program, Real -Time Marketing 
Automation were  successfully launched in Q3. All these initiatives will enhance business sales performance across 
all business groups, particularly in the domestic market, thereby supporting sustainable long -term growth.
•Continue to expand its brand portfolio to diversify revenue sources and reduce dependence on any single brand or 
business segment → new branch of F&B to launch in Q4 2025
•In the short term, the Q4 remains a period of strong operational performance, consistent with previous years, 
supported by the high tourism season and strong demand among its target customers.
